column3: NKJV has “sanctified by God the Father,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “beloved in God the Father.”
NKJV has “the only Lord God,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the only Master.”
NKJV has “though you once knew this, that the Lord,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “though you know all things, that the Lord once.”
NKJV has “on some have compassion, making a distinction,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “have mercy on those who doubt.”
NKJV has the shorter two-part form, following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has three groups, adding “to others show mercy with fear.”
NKJV has “who alone is wise” and lacks “through Jesus Christ our Lord, before all time,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks “wise” and includes those words.
